summary: Split egress paths after residency toggle causing APAC/EU asymmetric p95 latency
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported a sudden divergence in p95 latency across regions after enabling a residency control toggle. Some requests from EU routed to APAC egress, causing p95 spikes for EU traffic and elevated egress hop counts.

Impact: FinLedger saw increased p95 latency for user-facing features that query embeddings and completions. Approx 18% of requests originating in eu-west observed 400-700ms extra p95 tail and intermittent 429s when APAC pools were saturated. Business impact: degraded UX for enterprise trading dashboards (real-time indicators).

Environment: Dedicated deployment (FinLedger reserved pool), prod, apac-southeast-1 primary edge with eu-west-1 user base. Private control plane with VPC peering to customer network.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer toggled 'enforce_residency_lock' to true on their account via Console on 2026-03-02 23:41 UTC.
2) Traffic started to be steered by residency service; some requests still resolved to APAC egress due to stale DNS/edge affinity entries.
3) Observed p50 stable, p95 and p99 increased for affected prefixes.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 03-04 00:10 UTC: Customer reported p95 spikes. Support triaged and collected request IDs and headers.
- 03-04 00:25 UTC: SRE examined control-plane residency refresh logs; found residency-lock-refresh jobs for FinLedger ran at 23:43 and 23:53 but an error retried at 23:56 (internal rate limiter).
- 03-04 01:00 UTC: Correlated edge DNS cache records at apac-edge-04 and eu-edge-02; subset of edge nodes had cache TTLs extended to 600s due to previous emergency config change (hotfix) from 2026-02-28.
- 03-04 01:12 UTC: Traffic split ratio ~82% eu->eu egress, ~18% eu->apac egress for FinLedger prefixes.
- 03-04 01:35 UTC: APAC serving pool showed high memory pressure and queued requests leading to 429s under burst.

Technical findings:
- The residency state was updated in the control plane, but edge affinity persisted because of an emergency config that temporarily extended DNS cache TTLs for stability during prior maintenance. That TTL change was not scoped per-tenant and prevented timely failover.
- Control-plane retry of residency-lock-refresh was throttled due to a limiter that treated per-tenant refreshes as low-priority during global maintenance window.
- No authentication or IAM errors present.

Metrics examined:
- p95 latency for FinLedger from eu-west-1: baseline 120ms -> observed 520ms during peak window.
- egress hop_count metric showed group with hop_count=3 (multi-hop through apac) correlated with high p95.
- APAC pool CPU/mem: 85%/78% at spike.

comments: 2026-03-04 00:40 - Elena Park (Support): Acknowledged report and asked customer for sample request IDs and timestamps. Requested agreement to run control-plane trace for tenant.
2026-03-04 00:55 - SRE (Jonah Kim): Ran control-plane residency trace; saw refresh retry failures between 23:54-23:57 UTC due to rate limiter. Opened INT-403 for limiter side effects.
2026-03-04 01:20 - Customer (FinLedger - Alice Monroe): Confirmed residency toggle and shared that console reported a success state. Provided high-frequency logs for 00:20-00:30 UTC.

2026-03-04 02:05 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Temporarily forced per-tenant DNS flush for FinLedger on edge nodes to re-resolve egress. Noted immediate drop in eu->apac traffic from 18% to <1% and p95 returned to ~140ms. Recorded as mitigation action.

2026-03-06 09:12 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Rolled back the emergency global DNS TTL override and deployed scoped TTL fix to avoid cross-tenant side effects. Refer PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/276.
2026-03-10 11:23 - Elena Park (Support): Followed up with FinLedger to confirm UX recovered and asked to keep ticket open for 72h monitoring. Customer confirmed metrics stable and no user complaints.
resolution:
Mitigation: Forced per-tenant DNS cache flush on affected edge nodes which immediately re-aligned egress paths to eu pools and reduced p95. Fix: Rolled back the emergency global DNS TTL override and implemented tenant-scoped TTL behavior in the control plane. Also relaxed the residency-refresh rate limiter for tenant-critical refreshes during maintenance windows. Deployed patch (PR #276) to control-plane and edge config.

Status: Resolved for customer; monitoring continues for 72h. No further lateralized incidents observed.
follow_up_actions: Add an observability metric for per-tenant egress hop_count and alert when >1 for >5m
Introduce a runbook for residency toggle that includes a targeted cache-flush step
Adjust residency-refresh rate limiter to allow emergency per-tenant refreshes during maintenance windows
Postmortem/Confluence: author detailed incident analysis and link to runbook (RESP-449)
